title: The cave (1 Samuel 24)
hookLine: David could kill Saul while he sleeps, and cuts only the edge of his robe
carry: I will not lift my hand
last: A FRIEND CLOSER THAN A BROTHER.

cards: David and his men are crouched in the back of a cave in the wilderness of En-gedi, among the wild goats' rocks. Outside, King Saul is hunting him with an army.
Then the king himself walks in, alone, to relieve himself, with no idea who is sitting in the dark behind him.
One of David's men whispers what they're all thinking: this is the day the Lord promised, your enemy delivered into your hand. Do to him whatever seems good to you. David gets up.
He creeps forward with a blade.

teach.h: ONLY A CORNER OF THE ROBE.
teach.b: He cuts off a corner of Saul's robe. That's all. The king walks back into the light and never feels it.
Then a strange line, in the King James Bible: "David's heart smote him, because he had cut off Saul's skirt." Not for sparing him. For the cloth.
Even that small cut felt like too much.
He stops his men cold: "The LORD forbid that I should do this thing unto my master, the LORD's anointed, to stretch forth mine hand against him." Anointed is the key word.
Saul was anointed king with oil, and David will not be the one to remove him, even after spears thrown at his head, even with a promise of the throne. Then David does something brave.
He walks out after Saul and calls to him. He bows to the ground and holds up the corner of the robe as proof: I was close enough to kill you, and I didn't.

"I will not put forth mine hand against my lord; for he is the LORD's anointed." He leaves the judging to God. And Saul, the hunter, breaks: "Is this thy voice, my son David? And Saul lifted up his voice, and wept."

teach.h: THOU ART MORE RIGHTEOUS THAN I.
teach.b: He says it plainly: "Thou art more righteous than I." It doesn't last; Saul will hunt David again. What the cave shows is a man with every excuse and every chance, choosing not to take it.
Some Christians read this chapter beside Jesus's teaching to love enemies and Paul's line in Romans about leaving vengeance to God.

how: Some Christians read David sparing Saul in the cave alongside Jesus's teaching to love one's enemies, and the story is told in sermons and Sunday schools about refusing revenge.

games.q: you're David. the king who keeps trying to kill you is alone in the cave, his back to you. your men say: now. what do you do?
o: cut a corner from his robe and let him go.
stay hidden and do nothing at all.
games.why: he cuts only a corner of the robe, and even that troubles him. then he walks out and shows it to Saul as proof he spared him.

practice: Let someone who has wronged you come to mind, and notice the chance you have to get even: a remark you could repeat, a favor you could withhold.
Then picture David lowering his hand, holding only a scrap of cloth; you don't have to forgive everything today, just decide not to cut. If you pray, you can hand the judging to God in silence.
